### Before you file a bug report

- [x] I have checked the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues) and have not found an issue that matches the one I'm filing.
- [x] This issue is not a troubleshooting question. Troubleshooting questions go here: https://forum.mattermost.com/c/trouble-shoot/16.
- [x] This issue is not a feature request. You can request features and make product suggestions here: https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/.
- [x] This issue reproduces on one of the [currently supported server versions](https://docs.mattermost.com/about/mattermost-server-releases.html#latest-releases).
- [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Mattermost Handbook Contribution Guidelines](https://handbook.mattermost.com/contributors/contributors/guidelines/contribution-guidelines).

### Mattermost Server Version

11.10

### Operating System

Windows

### Steps to reproduce

  1. Set Windows OS to Dark Mode (Settings → Personalization → Colors → Choose your mode → Dark).
  2. Open the Mattermost Desktop App (theme syncing disabled — default).
  3. Switch Mattermost to Light Theme (Settings → Display → Theme → Denim or any light theme).
  4. Open any channel.
  5. Click in the message compose box and start typing.
  6. Observe: no visible text cursor in the input area.
  7. Click and drag to select text — the I-beam mouse cursor also disappears when hovering over the unselected (white) portion of the compose box

### Expected behavior

The text caret (blinking cursor) and I-beam mouse cursor are clearly visible in the message compose box regardless of the OS color scheme, because Mattermost is using a light theme with a white background.

### Observed behavior

In the light Mattermost theme, both the text caret and the I-beam mouse cursor appear white and are invisible against the white compose area background. The issue does not occur in the dark Mattermost theme. The issue does not occur in the browser (only in the desktop app). The cursor becomes briefly visible when text is selected (blue highlight provides contrast), but disappears again when moving into unselected white areas.

### Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Information

bug research by @claude:
```
    Root Cause

    The Mattermost Desktop App sets nativeTheme.themeSource = 'system'
    (themeManager.ts:182) when Theme Syncing is disabled (the default).

    On Windows with OS Dark Mode active, Electron/Chromium inherits the dark
    color scheme and renders native UI elements — including the text caret
    and I-beam cursor — in WHITE.
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Since the Mattermost light theme uses a white compose area                                                                                                                   
    (--center-channel-color-bg: #ffffff), both the caret and cursor                                                                                                              
    become invisible (white-on-white).                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    The dark theme is unaffected because its compose area is dark,                                                                                                               
    so a white cursor is visible. The browser is unaffected because it                                                                                                           
    is not an Electron app and does not inherit nativeTheme.                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Proposed Fixes (in order of preference)                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Fix 1 — webapp (utils.tsx, applyTheme function):                                                                                                                             
    Explicitly set color-scheme on <html> when applying a Mattermost theme,
    so Chromium always picks the correct cursor/caret color:                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                 
      const isLight = isLightColor(theme.centerChannelBg || '#ffffff');                                                                                                          
      document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = isLight ? 'light' : 'dark';                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Fix 2 — webapp CSS (wysiwyg_editor.scss and _post.scss):                                                                                                                     
    Explicitly set caret-color for all input areas so the text caret                                                                                                             
    is always the theme's text color regardless of color-scheme:                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                 
      .WysiwygEditor .ProseMirror {                                                                                                                                              
          caret-color: var(--center-channel-color);                                                                                                                              
      }                                                                                                                                                                          
      .app__body .custom-textarea {                                                                                                                                              
          caret-color: var(--center-channel-color);                                                                                                                              
      }                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Fix 3 — desktop app (themeManager.ts):                                                                                                                                       
    Extend the existing nativeTheme.themeSource sync logic
    (currently only runs when Config.themeSyncing is true) to also run                                                                                                           
    when theme syncing is disabled, so Electron always reflects the                                                                                                              
    actual Mattermost theme brightness.                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Fix 1 is the most complete: it fixes both the caret and the I-beam                                                                                                           
    cursor and works for all custom themes. Fix 2 addresses only the caret                                                                                                       
    but is a safe, minimal change. Fix 3 addresses the I-beam cursor                                                                                                             
    at the Electron level.                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Environment                                                                                                                                                                  
    - Mattermost version: 11.10.0                                                                                                                                                
    - Desktop app: affected (Electron, Windows)                                                                                                                                  
    - Browser: not affected                                                                                                                                                      
    - Mobile: not affected                                                                                                                                                       
    - OS requirement to reproduce: Windows in Dark Mode      
```
items.title: [Bug]: Invisible text cursor in light theme on Windows desktop app (OS dark mode conflict)

### Mattermost Server Version

11.10

### Operating System

MacOS

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any channel in the browser.
2. Have another user (or a bot) send a message to that channel.
3. Observe: the message does not appear in the channel view.
4. Navigate to another channel and back — the message is now visible.
5. Repeat step 2 from a different channel — the blue unread badge in the sidebar does not appear until F5

### Expected behavior

New messages appear immediately via WebSocket. The unread badge updates in real-time.

### Observed behavior

  **Observed behavior:**                                                   
  - A new message sent by another user does not appear in the currently open channel
  - The blue unread dot in the sidebar does not appear next to the channel name
  - Both issues resolve only after a manual action: navigating away and back (for messages) or refreshing the page (for the badge)
  - The problem does not occur in the desktop app or mobile client.

### Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Information

bug research by @claude:

```
  Suspected Root Causes

  Bug 1 — posts silently dropped:

  In webapp/channels/src/packages/mattermost-redux/src/reducers/entities/po
  sts.ts (around line 664):
                                                                           
  const postsForChannel = state[post.channel_id];
  if (!postsForChannel) {
      return state; // ← incoming WebSocket post is silently discarded
  }

  If postsInChannel for a channel is not yet initialized when a WebSocket
  posted event arrives, the post is dropped. Re-entering the channel
  triggers a fresh API fetch which recovers the message.

  Bug 2 — unread badge not re-rendered:                                    
  
  Memoized selectors (makeGetChannelUnreadCount in components/sidebar) may 
  not invalidate correctly when batched Redux actions are dispatched from
  completePostReceive (actions/new_post.ts:79). This interaction between   
  redux-batched-actions (v0.5.0, last updated 2019) and react-redux v9's
  useSyncExternalStore subscription model may prevent the sidebar from
  re-rendering.

  Both issues appear to be more pronounced since EnableConcurrentReact was 
  enabled server-wide.
                                                                           
  Environment                                                              
  
  - Mattermost version: 11.10.0                                            
  - Browser: Chrome / Firefox (both affected)
  - Desktop app: not affected                                              
  - Mobile: not affected
```
items.title: [Bug]: Real-time message delivery and unread badge broken on web client

### Mattermost Server Version

11.10.1

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect two Mattermost instances using Connected Workspaces.
2. Enable `TeamSettings.RestrictCreationToDomains` on the receiving workspace and include the remote user's actual email domain in the allowed list.
3. Share a channel between the workspaces.
4. Add a remote user whose real email belongs to the allowed remote domain.
5. Trigger shared-channel member synchronization.
6. Observe that the Remote Cluster remains healthy, but the remote user is not added to the local team/shared channel.
7. Check the receiving workspace logs and observe a `JoinUserToTeam` failure caused by domain validation.
8. Inspect the remote user on the receiving workspace and note that `users.email` contains a generated synthetic value while the actual email is stored in `props.RemoteEmail`.

### Expected behavior

A Connected Workspaces remote user whose real email belongs to a domain listed in `TeamSettings.RestrictCreationToDomains` should be successfully added to the local team and shared channel.

The synthetic local representation of the remote user's email should not cause domain validation to fail.

### Observed behavior

Shared-channel member synchronization fails during the local team membership step.

The remote user's actual email is preserved in `props.RemoteEmail`, while `users.email` contains a generated synthetic value without an email domain.

The team domain validation appears to be performed against `users.email`, causing the remote user to fail the domain check even though `props.RemoteEmail` belongs to a domain explicitly allowed by `TeamSettings.RestrictCreationToDomains`.

As a result, the remote user exists on the receiving workspace, but no corresponding team/channel membership is created.

### Log Output

```shell
Error upserting sync user
caller="sharedchannel/sync_recv.go:145"
remote=<remote>
channel_id=<channel_id>
user_id=<user_id>
error="error adding sync user to Team: JoinUserToTeam: the user cannot be added as the domain associated with the account is not permitted"

Failed to process membership change
caller="sharedchannel/membership_recv.go:79"
user_id=<user_id>
channel_id=<channel_id>
remote_id=<remote_cluster_id>
is_add=true
error="cannot upsert user for channel add: error adding sync user to Team: JoinUserToTeam: the user cannot be added as the domain associated with the account is not permitted"

Some membership changes failed
caller="sharedchannel/membership_recv.go:92"
```

### Additional Information

The team itself has no team-specific domain restriction: `teams.alloweddomains = ''`.

MM_FEATUREFLAGS_ENABLESHAREDCHANNELSDMS=true
MM_FEATUREFLAGS_ENABLESYNCALLUSERSFORREMOTECLUSTER=true
MM_FEATUREFLAGS_ENABLESHAREDCHANNELSMEMBERSYNC=true 
This parameters is enabled on both workspaces.

The remote user's actual domain is explicitly included in `TeamSettings.RestrictCreationToDomains`.

On the source workspace, the user has a normal email such as `user@remote.example.com`. On the receiving workspace, the same remote user is represented approximately as:

`users.email = <generated synthetic ID>`
`props.RemoteEmail = user@remote.example.com`

The Remote Cluster connection itself is healthy. The failure occurs specifically while adding the synchronized remote user to the receiving workspace team.

A possible fix would be to use `props.RemoteEmail` for domain-policy validation when the user is a Connected Workspaces remote user, while continuing to keep the synthetic value in `users.email`.

This seems preferable to bypassing `RestrictCreationToDomains` entirely, because the configured domain policy would still be enforced.
items.title: [Bug]: Connected Workspaces shared-channel member sync fails when RestrictCreationToDomains is enabled

### Mattermost Server Version

### Operating System

iOS (Safari) — also observed on mobile web (Chrome DevTools device emulation, viewport 390x844)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Mattermost in a mobile web browser (viewport ~390px wide, e.g. iPhone-sized).
2. Navigate into any channel that has messages spanning multiple days,
   where the most recent message is from day N (e.g. Friday) and the
   previous day with messages is day N-1 (e.g. Thursday).
3. Observe the sticky date divider that briefly appears at the top of
   the message list right after the channel loads.

### Expected behavior

The sticky date divider should always reflect the date of the message
currently in view. Since the view scrolls to and settles on the most
recent message (Friday), the divider should show "Friday" from the
moment it appears.

### Observed behavior

On initial channel load, the sticky date divider briefly shows the
previous day ("Thursday") instead of the actual most recent day
("Friday") of the message the view is scrolled to. It then disappears
after a moment, presumably once the scroll position settles — but the
date shown during that brief window is incorrect. This suggests the
divider is computed from an intermediate/incorrect scroll position
before the list finishes its initial virtualized scroll calculation.

Reproduced consistently across multiple channel entries in the same
workspace. Did not reproduce this specific timing issue when the

### Before you file a bug report

- [x] I have checked the issue tracker and have not found an issue that matches the one I'm filing.
- [x] This issue is not a troubleshooting question.
- [x] This issue is not a feature request.
- [x] This issue reproduces on one of the currently supported server versions.
- [x] I have read the contribution guidelines.

### Mattermost Server Version

11.8.2 (Enterprise build, no license). The code involved is unchanged on current `master`.

### Operating System

Debian 13 (trixie), arm64. Installed from the tarball, running under systemd.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Mattermost with the default file-based config (`config/config.json`).
2. Fill up the disk that `config/` lives on.
3. Restart Mattermost (or let systemd restart it).
4. Free up some disk space and start Mattermost again.

### Expected behavior

My existing `config.json` should survive. If Mattermost can't write the config, it should leave the old file alone. If it finds an empty config file on startup, it should fail and tell me, not assume it's a new install.

### Observed behavior

All of my config was gone. Mattermost started up with a fresh default config: `DataSource` pointed back at `mmuser:mostest@localhost/mattermost_test`, `SiteURL` was empty, plugin settings were gone, and so on. There was no backup, so I had to rebuild it by hand and reset the database password.

Here's what I think happens, from reading the code:

1. On every startup, `Store.Load` writes the config back to disk. On the first load it compares against an empty `model.Config{}`, so `hasChanged` is always true:
   https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/d16665723616ee8b63a127816cbad2022668354f/server/config/store.go#L320
2. `FileStore.persist` writes with `os.WriteFile`, which truncates the file before writing. If the write fails with ENOSPC, the truncate has already happened and `config.json` is left empty:
   https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/d16665723616ee8b63a127816cbad2022668354f/server/config/file.go#L120
3. On the next start the file is zero bytes. `Store.Load` doesn't treat that as an error. It just builds a default config and writes that out:
   https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/d16665723616ee8b63a127816cbad2022668354f/server/config/store.go#L259

So a full disk and a restart at the wrong moment is enough to silently reset the whole config.

### Log Output

```shell
# first start after the disk filled up
Sep 14 17:19:10 mattermost[843]: Error: failed to load configuration: failed to create store: unable to load on store creation: failed to persist: failed to write file: write /opt/mattermost/config/config.json: no space left on device
Sep 14 17:19:22 mattermost[3159]: Error: failed to load configuration: failed to create store: unable to load on store creation: failed to persist: failed to write file: write /opt/mattermost/config/config.json: no space left on device

# later starts, once there was some space again: running on the default config
{"level":"error","msg":"Failed to ping DB","caller":"sql/sql_utils.go:51","database":"master","dataSource":"postgres://****:****@localhost/mattermost_test?binary_parameters=yes&connect_timeout=10&sslmode=disable","error":"pq: password authentication failed for user \"mmuser\""}
```

### Additional Information

Two changes would each have prevented this:

- Write the config atomically: write to a temp file in the same directory, fsync, then rename it over `config.json`. A failed write then leaves the old file as it was.
- Refuse to start if `config.json` exists but is empty, instead of treating it like a missing file.

Not skipping the write-back on every startup would also shrink the window, but the first two are the real fix.

#27299 ("config.json wiped out") might be the same bug. It was closed because nobody could reproduce it.

Summary

After upgrading Mattermost Server to 11.10.1, users in a newly created private channel do not receive notifications for new messages.

When a new message is posted:

* The channel name becomes bold, indicating that Mattermost correctly detects the unread message.
* No desktop notification is shown.
* No notification sound is played.
* No unread notification dot/badge appears on the Mattermost Desktop App icon.

The issue affects all members of the private channel.

Mattermost version

Mattermost Enterprise Edition 11.10.1

Deployment: Kubernetes.

Steps to reproduce

1. Create a private channel.
2. Add multiple users to the channel.
3. Make sure the users have notifications enabled.
4. Have one user post a new message while another user is not viewing the channel.
5. Observe the receiving user’s Mattermost client.

Expected behavior

When a new message is posted:

* The channel should become bold/unread.
* A desktop notification should be displayed according to the user’s notification preferences.
* A notification sound should be played when enabled.
* The Mattermost Desktop App should indicate unread activity with a badge/dot.

Observed behavior

The channel becomes bold, so the unread state is detected correctly.

However:

* No desktop notification is displayed.
* No notification sound is played.
* No unread badge/dot appears on the Mattermost Desktop App icon.

Opening Mattermost shows the affected channel in bold.

Notification preferences

We checked the ChannelMembers.NotifyProps values in the database.

For the affected channel, users have normal/default channel notification settings, for example:

{
  "push": "default",
  "email": "default",
  "desktop": "default",
  "mark_unread": "all",
  "ignore_channel_mentions": "default"
}

The same notification settings are used in other channels.

We also verified the global Users.NotifyProps.

At least one affected user has:

{
  "desktop": "all",
  "desktop_sound": "true"
}

Therefore, this user should receive desktop notifications for all new messages.

Additional information

The problem was noticed after upgrading to Mattermost 11.10.1.

The important distinction is that unread state itself appears to work correctly: the channel becomes bold immediately when a new message arrives.

The problem appears to affect notification generation/display and the unread badge/dot.

We have not found channel-specific notification settings that would explain this behavior.

## Summary

Add a **"Send silently"** option for normal users when sending a message.

This would allow a user to send a message that is delivered normally, but does not trigger a desktop, mobile, or email notification for the recipient.

## Motivation

There are many situations where I want to send someone a message immediately, but I don't want to disturb them.

For example:

* Sending a work-related message outside working hours
* Sending a message on a weekend or holiday
* Sending something late at night so I don't forget about it
* Sending several messages while knowing the recipient will read them later

Currently, the alternatives are either:

* Wait until an appropriate time to send the message
* Send it normally and potentially disturb the recipient
* Schedule the message, which isn't always appropriate when I want the message to be available immediately

A per-message **"Send silently"** option would solve this cleanly.

## Existing support

Mattermost already has server-side support for silent posts. The current implementation allows bot accounts, OAuth apps, incoming webhooks, and plugins to create posts that are visible normally but don't produce notifications, unread badges, or the "New Messages" separator.

It would be great to expose this capability to normal users as well.

## Proposed UX

Add an option to the Send button, for example:

```text
Send ▼
  ├── Send
  └── Send silently
```

Or a keyboard shortcut could be provided as an alternative.

The message should otherwise behave like a normal message: it should be delivered immediately and remain visible in the conversation.

## Example

I'm working on Saturday and remember something I need to tell a colleague.

Instead of:

> "I'll send this on Monday."

or:

> Send now → colleague receives a notification on Saturday

I could choose:

> **Send silently**

The colleague would see the message normally when they next check Mattermost, without being disturbed at the time it was sent.

## Expected behavior

When "Send silently" is selected:

* The message is delivered immediately.
* The message appears normally in the conversation.
* No desktop notification is generated.
* No mobile push notification is generated.
* No email notification is generated.
* The recipient's notification settings are otherwise unchanged.
* The sender can choose this independently for each message.

This should be a per-message choice rather than a change to the recipient's notification preferences.

## Additional consideration

Since silent posts already exist for integrations, this feature could potentially reuse the existing server-side `silent` post mechanism rather than introducing a separate notification system.

The main product decision appears to be whether ordinary users should be permitted to use the existing capability and how it should be exposed in the UI.
items.title: Allow users to send individual posts without triggering notifications

**What it found.** The audit could not find a spacing token set here (it looks for `--space-*` / `--spacing-*` custom properties, Sass `$spacer` / `$spacing-*` variables and maps, or a Tailwind `--spacing` base), so it measured against a default 4px scale instead. Against that default it reported 1058 literal values, a number that says more about my token discovery than about your CSS, so I am not treating it as a finding.

If spacing is intentionally not on a scale, saying so is just as useful and I will mark the row that way.

The row for this repository will appear in a periodic "State of Spacing" table in the Rhythmguard repository, with this issue linked. If you would rather not be listed, say so here and I will remove it.

### Mattermost Server Version

master (dbf2899370, 2026-08-28)

### Operating System

Linux / macOS (server-side, OS independent)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a User Attributes (CPA) field of type `multiselect` with a single option.
2. `PATCH /api/v4/users/{user_id}/custom_profile_attributes` with that option ID repeated a few thousand times: `{"<field_id>": ["<option_id>", "<option_id>", ...]}`.
3. Do the same for a `multiuser` field with a few thousand distinct valid user IDs.
4. Read the values back with `GET /api/v4/users/{user_id}/custom_profile_attributes`.

Both are accepted and stored. I reproduced this against a local server through `PropertyService.UpsertPropertyValue` with the CPA validation hook registered — 5000 elements accepted for both types, and `["<option_id>", "<option_id>", "<option_id>"]` accepted for the duplicate case.

### Expected behavior

Array-typed CPA values are bounded the way scalar ones are, and a `select`-family field stores a set:

- a `multiselect` value cannot repeat the same option, and cannot hold more entries than the field has options;
- a `multiuser` value cannot repeat the same user, and has some upper bound on the number of entries.

### Observed behavior

Neither element count nor duplicates are checked. `validateValueAgainstField` verifies that every option ID exists and that every user ID is well formed, then stops:

https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/channels/app/properties/access_control_attribute_validation.go#L665-L700

Because a repeated option passes the existence check, a field with one single option is enough to store an arbitrarily long array. The contrast with the scalar path in the same function is what makes this look unintended: a `text` value is capped at 64 characters (`PropertyFieldValueTypeTextMaxLength`), roughly 256 bytes, while a `multiselect` value on the same user is limited only by the global request size — `ServiceSettings.MaximumPayloadSizeBytes`, 300 KB by default — with up to 50 values per patch request.

CPA values are broadcast to connected clients as a websocket event on every patch, so oversized values are re-sent rather than only stored.

### Log Output

_No response_

### Additional Information

Found while running property-based probes over the CPA value contract. Related: #36849 (the text limit was applied to bytes rather than characters).

I am happy to open a PR. The part I would like a steer on: should a duplicate be rejected with 400, or silently de-duplicated before storing? Rejecting is the stricter reading of "select", but it can break a client that already sends duplicates today.

### Summary

The Boards **person property** picker (card detail → Assignee) loads **only the first 10 team users** (one unpaginated API call) and offers no way to load more. On teams with more than 10 members, users whose username sorts alphabetically after the first page never appear in the dropdown — not even under a "Board members" group, and not even "Me" for the current user if they fall outside the first page.

They can only be reached by typing a search term, because the search path (`search=<term>`) re-queries the server and does not suffer from the page cap.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a team with >10 users (we have 44; ~10 of them active board members).
2. Open any board, open a card that has a **person** property (e.g. "Assignee").
3. Click the person value — the react-select dropdown opens.

### Expected behavior

- The dropdown lists all board members (and ideally team members with pagination or infinite scroll).
- "Me" is always offered.

### Observed behavior

The picker fires exactly one request:

```
GET /plugins/focalboard/api/v2/teams/{teamID}/users?search=&exclude_bots=true
```

which returns the first page of 10 users (alphabetical):

```
admin, aleksey, alenaef68, anastasiia, andrei, andreii.sivov,
borderlesscashflow, jvertugina, m.a.lozitskiy, maksitkov
```

The menu then groups these as "BOARD MEMBERS" / "NOT BOARD MEMBERS". Board members **mike, maxims, tatianabugrimova, valera** are absent — they sort after the first page and are never fetched.
- Scrolling the menu list to the bottom does **not** trigger a follow-up request.
- Pressing PageDown repeatedly does **not** trigger a follow-up request.
- Typing `mi` into the picker **does** find `mike` (search path works).

Selecting a searched user works fine and persists, so it is purely a loading/pagination gap in the widget, not a permissions or write problem.

### Environment

- Mattermost Server: **11.9.0** (Team Edition, Build 28847360617)
- Boards (focalboard) plugin: **9.3.1** bundled with 11.9.0
- Webapp in Chrome (Linux), also reproduced in headless Chromium via Playwright
- ~44 users in team, board shared with 10 members

### Additional context

Related prior reports (older server versions, likely same root cause):
- https://forum.mattermost.com/t/boards-can-not-add-team-members-to-person-property/13995
- https://github.com/mattermost/focalboard/issues/4376

Suggested fix directions: paginate/infinite-scroll the dropdown (e.g. react-select-async-paginate pattern), or have the picker explicitly fetch **all board members** (bounded set) before falling back to the team-wide paginated list.

Workaround for anyone hitting this: type the person's name into the picker — search bypasses the page cap.

### Expected behavior

### Summary

`MessageAttachment.IsValid()` accepts only `string` or `int64` for the `ts` field, but `Timestamp` is declared as `any` with no custom `UnmarshalJSON`. Go's `encoding/json` decodes JSON numbers into `float64` when the target is `any`, so **a numeric `ts` arriving over HTTP can never satisfy this check** — the `int64` branch is reachable only from Go callers constructing the struct directly.

Any Slack-compatible integration sending `"ts": 1234567890` triggers the warning on every message.

### Affected code

Post to any incoming webhook:

```json
}
```


### Observed behavior

This is not hypothetical or limited to hand-written integrations. **GitLab's built-in Mattermost notification service** sends `ts` as a bare JSON number, so every GitLab pipeline/issue notification produces this warning. The warning text says *"In a future version this will result in an error."* If that is enforced as currently written, it will reject GitLab notifications and every other Slack-style integration sending a numeric `ts`, since no JSON-encoded number can pass.

Accept `float64` (and optionally `json.Number`) in the type switch:


## Summary

`AtMentionProvider` can incorrectly stop sending user autocomplete requests for longer prefixes when the initial local-only lookup returns no results while the remote autocomplete request is still pending.

This is most visible when typing an out-of-channel user in `/invite @username`: only the first-character user autocomplete request is sent, while later input falls through to slash-command autocomplete and the intended user never appears.

## Environment

- Mattermost Server Team Edition: 11.5.1
- Mattermost Desktop: 6.2.2-rc.1 on macOS
- Database: PostgreSQL
- The same `lastPrefixWithNoResults` logic is still present in `v11.10.0` and `master` at the time of filing.

## Conditions that make the issue visible

1. The target user is not a member of the current channel.
2. No locally cached channel member, priority profile, group, or special mention matches the initial character.
3. The initial character matches more than 25 server-side users, and the target user is not in the first 25 results.
4. The user types the remaining characters before the initial autocomplete response completes. Network throttling makes this deterministic.

In one production trace, the initial character matched 124 users. The intended user ranked 90th, while the API request used `limit=25`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create or use a test/private channel that has no channel member whose username or profile name starts with `r`.
2. Choose a target user such as `rick.target` who is on the team but not in that channel.
3. Ensure the broad `r` search has more than 25 candidates and the target is outside the first 25 results.
4. Open browser/desktop DevTools and throttle the network, ideally adding 1–2 seconds of latency.
5. In the message box, type:

   ```text
   /invite @R
   ```

6. Wait until the following request is visible and still pending:

   ```text
   GET /api/v4/users/autocomplete?name=r&limit=25
   ```

7. Before that response completes, immediately type the remaining characters: `ick.target`.

## Expected behavior

User autocomplete should continue querying with the more specific prefixes, allowing the intended user to enter the top 25 results:

```text
users/autocomplete?name=r
users/autocomplete?name=ri
users/autocomplete?name=ric
users/autocomplete?name=rick
```

The target user should appear in the suggestion list.

## Observed behavior

Only the first-character user autocomplete request is sent. Later prefixes are handled by slash-command autocomplete instead:

```text
users/autocomplete?name=r
commands/autocomplete_suggestions?.../invite @Ri
commands/autocomplete_suggestions?.../invite @Ric
commands/autocomplete_suggestions?.../invite @Rick
```

The command autocomplete requests return no applicable user suggestions, so the target user does not appear.

Waiting for the `@R` request to finish before continuing, or pasting a sufficiently specific username at once, can avoid the issue.

## Root-cause analysis

In `AtMentionProvider.handlePretextChanged`, the provider renders the currently available local items before the remote user request completes:

https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/v11.5.1/webapp/channels/src/components/suggestion/at_mention_provider/at_mention_provider.tsx#L391-L438

The initial local-only call can contain no groups:

```ts
this.startNewRequest(prefix);
this.updateMatches(resultCallback, this.items(), matchedPretext);
```

`updateMatches` immediately treats that temporary local-only state as an authoritative no-result response:

```ts
if (groups.length === 0) {
    this.lastPrefixWithNoResults = this.latestPrefix;
}
```

When the next character is typed before the remote response completes, this check rejects the longer prefix and prevents another user autocomplete request:

```ts
if (this.lastPrefixWithNoResults && prefix.startsWith(this.lastPrefixWithNoResults)) {
    // Just give up since we know it won't return any results
    return false;
}
```

The assumption in the comment is only valid after an authoritative remote result is complete. At this point, only the partial local state has been checked.

Database or network latency increases the race window, but it is not the root cause: the missing `name=ri`, `name=ric`, and `name=rick` requests are never sent to the server. Artificial network throttling can reproduce the behavior with a healthy database.

The default client limit of 25 amplifies the user-visible impact because the stale broad-prefix response may not contain the intended user:

https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/v11.5.1/webapp/platform/client/src/client4.ts#L172-L176

## Current branch status

The same ordering and negative-prefix shortcut are present in:

- v11.5.1: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/v11.5.1/webapp/channels/src/components/suggestion/at_mention_provider/at_mention_provider.tsx#L377-L438
- v11.10.0: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/v11.10.0/webapp/channels/src/components/suggestion/at_mention_provider/at_mention_provider.tsx#L415-L479
- master: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/webapp/channels/src/components/suggestion/at_mention_provider/at_mention_provider.tsx#L415-L479

## Relevant history

The negative-prefix optimization was introduced as part of slash-command autocomplete work:

- https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-webapp/pull/5289
- https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-webapp/pull/5499
- https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-webapp/commit/31ef0489acbf844fd9997aa3a91f58423acaed0d

The local-first mention results architecture was introduced in:

- https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-webapp/pull/1974

## Suggested fix and regression test

Possible approaches:

1. Do not set `lastPrefixWithNoResults` from the initial local-only `updateMatches` call.
2. Set it only after both remote users and associated groups have completed for the current prefix.
3. Do not suppress a longer prefix while the request used to establish the no-result state is still pending.

A regression test could leave the `r` autocomplete promise unresolved, call `handlePretextChanged` again with `ri`, and assert that `autocompleteUsersInChannel` is called for both `r` and `ri`. It should also verify that a stale `r` response cannot replace the newer `ri` results.

### Summary

When `FileSettings.ExtractContent` is enabled and the bundled `pdftotext` is unavailable (see #36182 on distroless images), PDF text extraction falls back to the in-process Go parser `github.com/ledongthuc/pdf`, which the server ships via `replace => github.com/mattermost/pdf`. A **spec-valid** PDF whose page `/Contents` is an *array* of content streams, where a `TJ` array operand `[ ... ]` is split across a stream boundary (`[` at the end of one stream, its `]` at the start of the next), drives `(*buffer).readArray` into an infinite loop: at end-of-buffer `readToken()` keeps returning `io.EOF`, which `readArray` neither treats as a terminator nor stops on, so it appends forever → unbounded heap growth → `OOMKilled` (exit 137). CPU also saturates.

### Impact

Any user uploading such a PDF — or the hourly `extract_content` (catchup) job re-processing it — can OOM the mattermost container, and it recurs every time the job runs while the file is inside its lookback window. Reproduced on a 10.11.x build: a single **~93 KB, spec-valid** PDF grows the heap **~1.5 GB/s** until the container is OOM-killed.

### Root cause

1. `readArray` (`lex.go`) terminates only on `nil` / `keyword("]")`, not on `io.EOF`.
2. `Interpret` (`ps.go`) parses each stream of a `/Contents` array **separately** instead of concatenating them, so an array split across the boundary reaches EOF mid-array.

### Existing fix (unmerged upstream)

[`ledongthuc/pdf#58`](https://github.com/ledongthuc/pdf/pull/58) fixes both (an `io.EOF` break in `readArray` + `io.MultiReader` concatenation in `Interpret`); related: `ledongthuc/pdf` #64 / #76 / #79. Upstream `ledongthuc/pdf` appears unmaintained (last push 2025-05) and none of these are merged.

### Proposed fix

Port #58 into `github.com/mattermost/pdf` (the fork the server already uses via `replace`) and bump the server `go.mod`. Note the fork's `Interpret` has since gained a `context.Context` parameter, so the concatenation change needs to be adapted to that signature; `readArray` is unchanged from upstream and still affected. Happy to open a PR.

### Verification

With #58 applied to the fork revision the server currently pins, the previously-OOMing PDF extracts cleanly (`1739` bytes) with no memory growth; without it the heap grows without bound until OOM.

### Related

#36182 — broken `pdftotext` in distroless images, which is why extraction falls back to the in-process parser in the first place.

Post-quantum cryptography is getting more and more relevant. For example, Cloudlfare statistics show that post-quantum cryptography is already pretty popular on the Internet (https://radar.cloudflare.com/post-quantum).

**X25519MLKEM768**, in particular, is a key exchange algorithm that is supported in the TLS protocol and includes a classical (elliptic curve X25519) and a post-quantum (MLKEM768) part.

It has already been implemented in major OSS projects, including Mozilla Firefox (https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/132.0/releasenotes/) and OpenSSL (https://openssl-library.org/news/openssl-3.5-notes/).

Providing support for post-quantum cryptography will help keeping up with this trend and increasing security, especially for people accessing Mattermost from an already post-quantum-capable browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, ...).

From a technical standpoint, Mattermost uses Golang for the Server component. 

This is already pretty good, because Golang does support X25519MLKEM768 since 1.24, but it is possible that this feature is not used or enabled by the Mattermost Server code.

If you find this interesting, I can deal with the Server part. 

I am not sure whether additional components need some changes to ensure this feature is supported in all use cases.

## Summary

Update the `timezones.json` dependency used by the web app from `1.7.1` to `1.7.2`.

## Context

An implementation PR already exists: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/37412

That PR updates the timezone metadata dependency in `webapp/channels/package.json`. I am creating this issue so the work can be tracked independently and picked up or completed while contributor approval/CLA status is still pending for the original PR author.

## Why this matters

Mattermost uses this metadata to render timezone labels in the user settings UI. The older metadata package can contain outdated labels and offsets for some IANA timezone mappings.

Browser timezone detection and timestamp calculations use separate APIs/libraries, so this should be a narrow metadata refresh rather than a change to Mattermost timezone handling logic.

Update:

- `timezones.json`: `1.7.1` -> `1.7.2`

## Testing

A quick spot-check should be enough:

- Open user settings.

With S3-backed storage this may fail with HTTP 400 when the plugin leaves the file unchanged and does not write anything to `output`. This affects plugins such as `mattermost-community/mattermost-plugin-antivirus`, which only reads the uploaded file stream for scanning and intentionally ignores the replacement `output io.Writer`. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure Mattermost with S3-compatible file storage. 2. Install and enable a `FileWillBeUploaded` plugin that scans the uploaded file but does not modify it. Example: `mattermost-community/mattermost-plugin-antivirus`. 3. Upload a safe/non-infected file. 4. Observe that the plugin scans the file successfully and returns an empty rejection reason. 5. Mattermost still attempts to write `.tmp` via the file backend. 6. With S3 storage, this can fail with HTTP 400 from `PutObject`. ## Actual behavior Why this is problematic for S3 For S3 storage, WriteFile calls PutObject: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/9e3d8efc1a62b53e883a5a08ce3552c7c9fc896d/server/platform/shared/filestore/s3store.go#L522-L557 When the input is an io.PipeReader, the object size is unknown: objSize := int64(-1) ... info, err := b.client.PutObject(ctx, b.bucket, path, fr, objSize, options) If the plugin did not write to output, the pipe produces zero bytes. Some S3-compatible backends may reject this empty unknown-size upload with HTTP 400. Example plugin behavior mattermost-community/mattermost-plugin-antivirus scans the file and ignores output: https://github.com/mattermost-community/mattermost-plugin-antivirus/blob/872708a3742d166b7328cd5345dba32d25d649cc/server/plugin.go#L22-L65 Relevant behavior: response, err := av.ScanStream(file, abortScan) ... if !ok { return info, "" } The plugin does not modify the file contents, so Mattermost should not attempt to create or upload a replacement .tmp object. Possible root cause runPluginsHook uses the same streaming path for both cases: plugin writes replacement content to output; plugin leaves output untouched. Because Mattermost calls a.WriteFile(r, tmpPath) before knowing whether the plugin wrote any bytes, unchanged uploads still perform a backend write. There is also a related edge case: WriteFile(r, tmpPath) is handled before reading errChan. If a plugin rejects the upload but the empty .tmp write fails first, the rejection reason may be masked by the storage error, and cleanup of the original uploaded object may not run through the rejection path. Suggested fix Avoid calling WriteFile for the temporary replacement object until at least one byte is actually received from the plugin output pipe. One possible approach: Run the hook as today. Read/probe the first byte from the pipe. If EOF is reached before any bytes are read:check errChan; if there is no rejection, treat the file as unchanged; do not call WriteFile; do not create .tmp. If at least one byte is read:write io.MultiReader(bytes.NewReader(firstByte), r) to .tmp; then move it over the original as today. Pseudo-code sketch: var first [1]byte n, readErr := r.Read(first[:]) if readErr == io.EOF && n == 0 { if err = <-errChan; err != nil { if fileErr := a.RemoveFile(info.Path); fileErr != nil { rctx.Logger().Warn("Failed to remove file", mlog.Err(fileErr)) } return err } // Plugin did not write replacement content. // File is unchanged; do not create/write tmp object. return nil } if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF { r.CloseWithError(readErr) return model.NewAppError("runPluginsHook", "app.upload.run_plugins_hook.read_fail", nil, "", http.StatusInternalServerError).Wrap(readErr) } tmpPath := filePath + ".tmp" written, err := a.WriteFile(io.MultiReader(bytes.NewReader(first[:n]), r), tmpPath) Environment Mattermost version: 11.5.2 File storage: S3-compatible backend (yandex s3 object storage) Plugin: mattermost-community/mattermost-plugin-antivirus Plugin commit: 872708a3742d166b7328cd5345dba32d25d649cc Mattermost code reference checked against commit: 9e3d8efc1a62b53e883a5a08ce3552c7c9fc896d ### Expected behavior If a `FileWillBeUploaded` plugin does not write to `output`, Mattermost should treat the file as unchanged and continue the upload without attempting to write a replacement `.tmp` object. Per the hook contract: > To allow the file without modification, do not write to the output and return a nil *model.FileInfo and an empty string. Reference: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/9e3d8efc1a62b53e883a5a08ce3552c7c9fc896d/server/public/plugin/hooks.go#L280-L291 ### Observed behavior For S3 storage, WriteFile calls PutObject: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/9e3d8efc1a62b53e883a5a08ce3552c7c9fc896d/server/platform/shared/filestore/s3store.go#L522-L557 When the input is an io.PipeReader, the object size is unknown: objSize := int64(-1) ... info, err := b.client.PutObject(ctx, b.bucket, path, fr, objSize, options) If the plugin did not write to output, the pipe produces zero bytes. N/A — this is a client npm package issue, not a server issue

## Operating System

Any

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install TypeScript 6 in your project
2. Add `@mattermost/client@11.9.0` as a dependency
3. Run a build or type-check

## Expected behavior

`@mattermost/client` should work correctly with TypeScript 6, as it is a stable major release of the compiler.

## Observed behavior

npm/pnpm/yarn reports an unmet peer dependency warning, and type-checking may fail due to version range mismatch.

In [`webapp/platform/client/package.json`](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/webapp/platform/client/package.json#L31), the `peerDependencies` range is:

```json
"typescript": "^4.3.0 || ^5.0.0"
```

And `devDependencies` is pinned to:

```json
"typescript": "^5.0.0"
```

Neither range covers TypeScript `^6.0.0`.

## Log Output

```
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn peer dep missing: typescript@^4.3.0 || ^5.0.0, required by @mattermost/client@11.9.0
```

## Additional Information

The fix is straightforward — expand both ranges:
- `peerDependencies`: `"^4.3.0 || ^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0"`
- `devDependencies`: bump to `^6.0.0` and run CI against TypeScript 6

Hello and thank you for this great platform, 
I would like to propose ( in order to increase supply chain security of the project) to use StageX(https://stagex.tools/) for deterministic, verifiable builds.
StageX is a minimal, fully bootstrapped, and reproducible Linux distribution designed for verifiable infrastructure—which I believe could provide significant benefits to the Mattermost project:
Key Advantages:
Reproducible Builds
    Every build produces bit-for-bit identical artifacts, making it easy to verify release integrity
    Users can rebuild Mattermost at any time and compare hashes to detect compromises
Supply Chain Security
    Full-source bootstrapped from a 190-byte seed (no unverified binaries in the dependency chain)
    Multi-party cryptographic signing on all artifacts with hardware-backed PGP keys
    Protection against compromised or malicious (stagex)maintainers
OCI-Native Design
    Seamless integration with modern container workflows via Open Container Initiative standards
    Package locking for deterministic dependencies
    Compatible with existing Containerfile workflows
Trust Model
    Decentralized trust: no single point of failure for infrastructure security
    Already adopted by other organizations (Mysten Labs, Zcash, BitGo, Uniswap Labs, Talos Linux)

Even if you don't want to use it to build everything with stageX you can start by using it only for the go binaries!
Go is a first class citizen in stagex, compiled early in the bootstrap chain!
Currently I have been fiddling with a Containerfile to fully build Mattermost (thus also react etc) but it is a bit of a struggle.
Still I provide here my Containerfile that you can get inspiration, an possibly could be of use to you!
The first part is not compiling fully yet, but the server part is fully functional!

Consider that a `sources` folder has to exit to provide the tar archive. (the containerfile was made with help from llm!)
```
# ── Stage: source (Mattermost source from local cache) ─────
FROM docker.io/stagex/core-busybox@sha256:3d3898e4a0ac62e1e671092c407fc611fb9a8df15d2a431047868ee2ec034a67 AS source

USER root

ARG MATTERMOST_VERSION=v11.7.2

COPY sources/mattermost-v11.7.2.tar.gz /tmp/
RUN mkdir -p /src/mattermost && tar xzf /tmp/mattermost-v11.7.2.tar.gz -C /src/mattermost --strip-components=1

# ── Stage: webapp (build frontend with StageX toolchain) ──
# Uses pallet-clang-gnu-busybox for working clang+make+libc++,
# adds python3 from pallet-python (needed by node-gyp for native addons),
# and copies node/npm from pallet-nodejs.
FROM docker.io/stagex/pallet-clang-gnu-busybox@sha256:f158aeecd0e2461d45c70ff56ee57cbcd1e4e6706babfc665414f9e641410e6a AS webapp-builder

# Python 3 (node-gyp dependency)
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-python@sha256:d189a8e4f3bb9d9518258cc2d4a1c7cfe7d4bd6cb6ebedcf066eb26eafecb62a . /

# Node.js runtime + npm
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /usr/bin/node /usr/bin/node
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /usr/lib/node_modules /usr/lib/node_modules
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libbrotli* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libcares* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libnghttp2* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libicudata* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libicui18n* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libicuuc* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libcrypto.so* /lib/
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /lib/libssl.so* /lib/

# Git + CA certs: needed by npm 11.x for git dependencies with HTTPS.
# core-git provides the git binary; core-ca-certificates provides the CA
# bundle for TLS verification. SSL_CERT_FILE tells Node.js where to find
# the system CA store (StageX's Node build doesn't bundle Mozilla certs).
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/core-git@sha256:371a0307a65821b60986a150db4e18bb6b76ed6d4977d9bbcd4aed6a37d05014 /usr/bin/git /usr/bin/git

ENV SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

# Create npm/npx symlinks (COPY resolves symlinks)
RUN ln -s /usr/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js /usr/bin/npm && \
    ln -s /usr/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npx-cli.js /usr/bin/npx

# Provide libgcc_s.so.1 — clang needs this for linking
RUN ln -s libunwind.so /usr/lib/libgcc_s.so.1

# Copy Node.js headers so node-gyp can rebuild native addons offline.
# (Currently unused — we stub lmdb and @parcel/watcher instead of rebuilding,
#  but kept for future if other native addons need compilation.)
COPY --from=docker.io/stagex/pallet-nodejs@sha256:65edb5c0274be861053f033cd395f36fed3177110a8317027a3c4727007bd3a4 /usr/include/node /usr/include/node

# The base image (pallet-clang-gnu-busybox) sets CC=clang etc. via /etc/profile
# and SHELL ["/bin/sh","-l","-c"], but Podman's OCI format ignores SHELL, so
# the profile never gets sourced. Set the compiler vars explicitly so node-gyp
# (used by npm rebuild for native addons) finds them regardless.
ENV CC=clang
ENV CXX=clang++
ENV LD=ld.mold

# SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH tells build tools to use a fixed timestamp for
# reproducible output (respected by Rollup, node-gyp, etc.)
ENV SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1

WORKDIR /src
COPY --from=source /src/mattermost/webapp ./

# Patch package-lock.json: replace SSH URLs with HTTPS (npm 11.x can't handle
# git+ssh://, and the container has no SSH keys anyway). Also configure git to
# rewrite SSH-style refs to HTTPS as a fallback for any remaining git deps.
RUN sed -i 's|git+ssh://git@github.com/|git+https://github.com/|g' package-lock.json && \
    sed -i 's|ssh://git@github.com/|https://github.com/|g' package-lock.json && \
    git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf ssh://git@github.com/ && \
    git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com:

# npm ci --ignore-scripts: install deps without running postinstall.
# Then apply project patches (patch-package), then stub lmdb and
# @parcel/watcher — both ship pre-built .node binaries incompatible
# with Node.js v25's V8/libstdc++. Replace their JS entry points
# with no-op stubs (lmdb only used for Parcel cache, watcher only
# for dev file watching — neither is needed during `parcel build`).
# Finally build platform workspaces.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \
    npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefer-offline --fetch-timeout=300000 --fetch-retries=5 --fetch-retry-mintimeout=20000 && \
    npx patch-package && \
    cd node_modules/lmdb && \
    rm -f dist/index.cjs dist/index.mjs && \
    node -e "const f=require('fs'); f.writeFileSync('dist/index.cjs', 'const m={get:()=>{},put:()=>{},remove:()=>{},close:()=>{},transaction:f=>f(),getValues:()=>[]};module.exports={open:()=>m};')" && \
    node -e "const f=require('fs'); f.writeFileSync('dist/index.mjs', 'const m={get:()=>{},put:()=>{},remove:()=>{},close:()=>{},transaction:f=>f(),getValues:()=>[]};export const open=()=>m;')" && \
    cd /src/node_modules/@parcel/watcher-linux-x64-musl && \
    rm -f watcher.node && \
    node -e "const f=require('fs'); f.writeFileSync('index.js', 'module.exports={subscribe:()=>Promise.resolve({unsubscribe:()=>{}}),unsubscribe:()=>{},getEventsSince:()=>Promise.resolve([]),writeSnapshot:()=>Promise.resolve([])};\n')" && \
    node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); p.main='index.js'; require('fs').writeFileSync('package.json', JSON.stringify(p,null,2)+'\n')" && \
    cd /src && \
    npm run build --workspace platform/types \
                  --workspace platform/client \
                  --workspace platform/components \
                  --workspace platform/shared

# Patch the only(-maybe-) non-reproducible element in webpack:
# Date.now() produces different values on each build, embedded as cache-bust
# query param ?bt=<ts> in module federation remote entry URLs.
# Fixed value has no functional impact — it's just a cache buster.
RUN sed -i 's/const buildTimestamp = Date.now();/const buildTimestamp = 1;/' channels/webpack.config.js && \
    npm run build

# ── Stage: build (Mattermost server from source) ──
FROM docker.io/stagex/pallet-go@sha256:da52b0cea8cd9b7a5dd12a4bfbcfca32725d69b78d0c921bfbcd72412ba043ae AS build

WORKDIR /src
COPY --from=source /src/mattermost /src/mattermost

# Build Mattermost server (fully static, no CGO)
# server/public is an internal module needing a local replace.
# Check first to avoid duplicating on cached builds.
WORKDIR /src/mattermost/server
RUN grep -qxF 'replace github.com/mattermost/mattermost/server/public => ./public' go.mod 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "replace github.com/mattermost/mattermost/server/public => ./public" >> go.mod && \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=on \
    go mod download

RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=on \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -buildid=" \
    -o /usr/bin/mattermost ./cmd/mattermost

# ── Stage: rootfs (prepare runtime filesystem with correct permissions) ──
# We prepare /rootfs here because stagex/core-filesystem has no shell/busybox.
FROM docker.io/stagex/core-busybox@sha256:3d3898e4a0ac62e1e671092c407fc611fb9a8df15d2a431047868ee2ec034a67 AS rootfs

# Create runtime directory structure under /rootfs
RUN mkdir -p /rootfs/usr/bin \
             /rootfs/mattermost/config \
             /rootfs/mattermost/data \
             /rootfs/mattermost/logs \
             /rootfs/mattermost/plugins \
             /rootfs/mattermost/client/plugins \
             /rootfs/usr/i18n

# Copy the compiled Go binary
COPY --from=build /usr/bin/mattermost /rootfs/usr/bin/mattermost

# Copy i18n translation files from source
# FindDirRelBinary("i18n") searches ../i18n from /usr/bin → /usr/i18n
COPY --from=source /src/mattermost/server/i18n /rootfs/usr/i18n

# Copy email templates from source
# FindDirRelBinary("templates") searches ../templates from /usr/bin → /usr/templates
COPY --from=source /src/mattermost/server/templates /rootfs/usr/templates

# Set permissions:
# - Binary should be executable
# - Runtime dirs (data, logs, plugins, config) are mount points for volumes
#   or need runtime writes; make them 777 for safety
# - Ownership is root (UID 0) by default — the container will run as root,
#   but in rootless podman, container UID 0 maps to the unprivileged host user,
#   so there's no actual privilege escalation
RUN chmod 755 /rootfs/usr/bin/mattermost && \
    chmod 777 /rootfs/mattermost/data /rootfs/mattermost/logs \
             /rootfs/mattermost/plugins /rootfs/mattermost/client/plugins \
             /rootfs/mattermost/config

# ── Stage: package (minimal stagex runtime — no shell, no bash) ──
# This is the ONLY image that ships. It uses stagex/core-ca-certificates which
# is built on top of stagex/core-filesystem (basic directory structure + users)
# and adds CA certificates for TLS verification.
FROM docker.io/stagex/core-ca-certificates@sha256:7773dae6630aa3bdcc82cfec6c9265c0c501aaf0af67cc73631b09e1cff1b094 AS package

# Copy the prepared rootfs — ownership and permissions preserved from build stage
COPY --from=rootfs /rootfs/ /

# Copy the webapp client (built from source in StageX webapp-builder)
COPY --from=webapp-builder /src/channels/dist /mattermost/client

EXPOSE 8065 8067 8074 8075

# Set working directory to /mattermost (contains config/, data/, logs/)
WORKDIR /mattermost

# When MM_CONFIG is set and the file does not exist, Mattermost generates a
# default config.json from embedded defaults + environment variable overrides.
ENV MM_CONFIG=/mattermost/config/config.json

# The container runs as root (UID 0). In rootless podman, only container UID 0
# is mapped to the host user — all other UIDs are unmapped and get EPERM on
# volume writes. Running as root inside the container is safe because:
# 1. Rootless podman maps container UID 0 → host UID (unprivileged)
# 2. The host kernel enforces host user's permissions, not root
# 3. The stagex image provides no elevation tools (no sudo, no su, no binaries
#    except the Mattermost server itself)
USER 0
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/mattermost"]
CMD ["server"]

```

### Before you file a bug report

- [x] I have checked the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues) and have not found an issue that matches the one I'm filing.
- [x] This issue is not a troubleshooting question. Troubleshooting questions go here: https://forum.mattermost.com/c/trouble-shoot/16.
- [x] This issue is not a feature request. You can request features and make product suggestions here: https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/.
- [x] This issue reproduces on one of the [currently supported server versions](https://docs.mattermost.com/about/mattermost-server-releases.html#latest-releases).
- [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Mattermost Handbook Contribution Guidelines](https://handbook.mattermost.com/contributors/contributors/guidelines/contribution-guidelines).

### Mattermost Server Version

11.7.1

### Operating System

Ubuntu Server 24.04

### Steps to reproduce

In AD/LDAP attribute mapping for Custom Profile Attributes (CPA), map the AD attribute department to a Mattermost CPA field of type text (in our case the field ID is bpf53rxfwjgs8pdmof4gn8psfw, attribute name department).

In Active Directory, set the user's Department attribute to a value that is 53 Cyrillic characters long, for example:
Развитие и оценка компетенций по работе с клиентами
(52–53 characters depending on trailing space; ~97 bytes in UTF-8).

Have the user log in to Mattermost via SAML SSO. CPA values are pulled from AD during login and pushed through PatchCPAValues.

Observe the result: the user logs in, but the department attribute is not updated in the Mattermost profile, and an error is written to mattermost.log (see Log Output below).
Shorten the AD Department value to ~40 characters or fewer and repeat the login — the value is now successfully synced to the Mattermost profile.

### Expected behavior

According to the official Mattermost documentation for Custom Profile Attributes, "Values can be up to 64 characters long". The word characters implies Unicode code points (runes), not bytes.

Therefore the value Развитие и оценка компетенций по работе с клиентами (52 characters) should be accepted and synced from AD to the Mattermost user profile, exactly the same way a 52-character Latin string would be accepted.

In general, any text value of up to 64 Unicode characters, regardless of script (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, CJK, emoji), should pass validation, matching the documented contract.

### Observed behavior

The CPA text validator rejects the value with value too long, even though the string is only 52–53 characters long (well below the documented 64-character limit).

The limit is in fact applied in bytes, not in characters. For UTF-8:

Latin character = 1 byte → 64 characters fit.
Cyrillic character = 2 bytes → effective limit ≈ 32 characters.
CJK / emoji = 3–4 bytes → effective limit ≈ 16–21 characters.
The 52-character Cyrillic string from AD is 97 bytes in UTF-8, so it exceeds the byte-based limit and is rejected, even though it is well within 64 characters.

Confirmation that this is enforced in Go code, not in the database:

DB column propertyvalues.value is jsonb with no length limit.
The failing INSERT/UPDATE never reaches PostgreSQL — the error is returned by the application before the DB call.
This is consistent with PR #30694 (MM-63654 / MM-63721), which introduced the 64 limit for CPA text fields. The implementation appears to use len(value) (byte length in Go) instead of utf8.RuneCountInString(value) (rune/character count).
Impact: AD/LDAP department (and any other CPA text attribute) cannot be synced for non-Latin locales with realistic department names. In our deployment this affects a large portion of users whose department names in AD are standard Russian phrases of 35–60 characters. The only workaround today is to shorten the value in AD, which is not acceptable as a long-term solution because AD is the source of truth for HR data.

Suggested fix: Replace the byte-length check with a rune count in the CPA text validator (likely server/public/model/custom_profile_attributes.go or the corresponding PatchCPAValues validation path introduced in PR #30694), e.g. use utf8.RuneCountInString(value) <= 64 instead of len(value) <= 64. Optionally update the documentation if the intent really is "64 bytes", but the user-facing contract clearly states characters.



### Log Output

```shell
id=zfsh3735bbb1dd79dq6at1ueyc ip_addr=10.2.16.99 user_id= method=POST user_id=8md3e6k14frr5kn7i5htw6qtaw failed_count=1 errors="1 error(s) updating CPA values: Failed to update field bpf53rxfwjgs8pdmof4gn8psfw with attribute department: PatchCPAValues: Не удалось проверить значение свойства, value too long"
```

### Additional Information

_No response_
items.title: [Bug]: CPA text field length limit is enforced in bytes instead of characters, breaking AD sync for non-Latin locales

2. Ensure zh-CN is added to the TargetLanguages in config.json.
3. Set a user's profile language to "Chinese (Simplified)".
4. Have another user post an English message in a channel where auto-translate is enabled.


### Expected behavior

Mattermost should request the translation from LibreTranslate using a compatible locale code (like zh-Hans or zh), receive the translation, and store it in the database.

### Observed behavior

The translation completely fails. Mattermost sends the literal zh-CN locale code to the LibreTranslate API. LibreTranslate follows the BCP 47 standard more strictly for Chinese, expecting zh-Hans (or its internal alias zh), and returns an error because it does not recognize zh-CN. Mattermost does not map this code internally before making the API call.

### Log Output

```shell
{"timestamp":"2026-05-15 07:59:45.494 +02:00","level":"error","msg":"Auto-translation operation failed","caller":"autotranslation/helpers.go:84","operation":"getOrCreateTranslation.createTranslation","object_type":"post","object_id":"j7zxyf1f33b6ind7qihrhw1tre","dst_lang":"zh-CN","error":"AutoTranslationImpl.getOrCreateTranslation: Die Übersetzung konnte nicht erstellt werden., translation error [provider=libretranslate]: language not supported by provider"}
```

I verified this by manually adding zh-CN as an alias mapped to zh-Hans inside the LibreTranslate server's python source code. Once we did that, the backend integration worked flawlessly, and Mattermost successfully received and stored the translation in its database. ## Summary

A handful of mmctl subcommands explicitly disable local mode via `disableLocalPrecheck` and exit with `"This command cannot be run in local mode"`:

- `mmctl bot create`
- `mmctl token generate` (also reached via `bot create --with-token`)

The local-mode socket is the natural way to provision a Mattermost server from a deployment script — authenticated by filesystem permissions on the Unix socket rather than by a logged-in admin session, ideal for first-run automation where no admin credentials yet exist. Most provisioning steps (`team create`, `channel create`, `user create`, `config set`, …) work fine through `--local`.

The `bot create` / `token generate` exception forces automated bootstraps into a less-clean dance: create an admin user, log in over REST with that user's password, create the bot, mint a PAT, only then enable + enforce MFA. During that window the admin account is reachable with password alone — a real, if narrow, security exposure that wouldn't exist if `--local` covered the bot/token path.

## Mattermost Server Version

Verified against `master` (`server/cmd/mmctl/commands/bot.go`, current as of filing). The `PreRun: disableLocalPrecheck` gate has been in place across recent 9.x / 10.x releases.

## Operating System

Reproduces on Linux (any distro running the official `mattermost/mattermost-team-edition` container with local mode enabled).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Bring up a Mattermost server with `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_ENABLELOCALMODE=true` and `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_LOCALMODESOCKETLOCATION` set.
2. From a process with read/write access to the local-mode socket:
   ```
   mmctl --local bot create testbot
   ```

## Expected behavior

mmctl creates the bot account through the local-mode socket, mirroring how `mmctl --local user create`, `team create`, and `channel create` already work.

## Observed behavior

```
$ mmctl --local bot create testbot
This command cannot be run in local mode
$ echo $?
1
```

Source: `server/cmd/mmctl/commands/bot.go` — `CreateBotCmd` carries `PreRun: disableLocalPrecheck`. The same gate covers the token-generation path reached via `bot create --with-token`.

## Additional Information

**Request:** drop the `disableLocalPrecheck` PreRun on `CreateBotCmd` (and the token-generation path) so `--local` covers them, or document the rationale for excluding them so deployers can plan around the gap.

**Concrete impact on first-run automation:** the gap forces this ordering — admin created → admin logs in over REST with password → bot + token created → MFA enforced. Until the last step, the admin is reachable with password alone via whatever public ingress the deployment exposes. Local-mode coverage would let the entire provisioning flow finish before any password-authenticated REST endpoint is required.
items.title: mmctl --local: support `bot create` and `token generate`

### Mattermost Server Version

11.6.0 (build 24038116943). Also present on `master` as of the time of filing.

### Operating System

Server: Linux (TrueNAS SCALE ix-app Docker image). Affected clients: Mattermost Mobile for Android 2.39.0 (iOS likely same, not verified).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install any webapp-enabled plugin on a Mattermost 11.x server (reproduced with `com.mattermost.calls` 1.11.4, `mattermost-ai` 1.7.2, `com.github.manland.mattermost-plugin-gitlab` 1.12.1).
2. `curl https://<host>/api/v4/plugins/webapp` and note the `webapp.bundle_path` returned for every plugin — it is of the form `/static/<plugin_id>/<plugin_id>_<hash>_bundle.js`.
3. `curl -I https://<host>/static/<plugin_id>/<plugin_id>_<hash>_bundle.js` — returns **404**.
4. `curl -I https://<host>/static/plugins/<plugin_id>/<plugin_id>_<hash>_bundle.js` — returns **200**.
5. On the Android mobile app, attempt to join a Calls channel call — UI renders a blank screen without controls (the native Calls screen depends on the webapp plugin bundle loading successfully for some of its state).

### Expected behavior

`GET /api/v4/plugins/webapp` should return `bundle_path` that resolves on the server — i.e. `/static/plugins/<plugin_id>/<bundle>`. All clients consuming the manifest verbatim should then load the bundle successfully.

### Observed behavior

`bundle_path` is `/static/<plugin_id>/<bundle>` (missing the `/plugins/` segment). The path 404s because the static file handler at `/static/` serves from the webapp client directory, while plugin bundles live under `/static/plugins/` (served from `PluginSettings.ClientDirectory`). The desktop webapp silently rewrites the path client-side, hiding the bug; mobile clients take the manifest value verbatim and fail.

### Log Output

N/A — no server-side errors; failing request is a 404 with no log entry.

### Additional Information

**Source references (current `master`):**

1. `server/public/model/manifest.go:263` — `Manifest.ClientManifest()` builds the bad path:
   ```go
   cm.Webapp.BundlePath = "/static/" + m.Id + "/" + fmt.Sprintf("%s_%x_bundle.js", m.Id, m.Webapp.BundleHash)
   ```
   Should be `"/static/plugins/" + m.Id + "/" + ...`.

2. `server/channels/web/static.go:39–47` — the HTTP routes prove plugin bundles are only reachable under `/static/plugins/`:
   ```go
   staticHandler := ... http.FileServer(http.Dir(staticDir))                               // webapp static
   pluginHandler := ... http.FileServer(http.Dir(*w.srv.Config().PluginSettings.ClientDirectory))
   w.MainRouter.PathPrefix("/static/plugins/").Handler(pluginHandler)
   w.MainRouter.PathPrefix("/static/").Handler(staticHandler)
   ```

3. `webapp/channels/src/plugins/index.ts:167–171` — desktop webapp already compensates, comment says *"Backwards compatibility for old plugins"*:
   ```ts
   let bundlePath = manifest.webapp?.bundle_path;
   if (bundlePath && bundlePath.includes('/static/') && !bundlePath.includes('/static/plugins/')) {
       bundlePath = bundlePath.replace('/static/', '/static/plugins/');
   }
   ```

**Impact surface:** every non-webapp client that consumes `/api/v4/plugins/webapp` and uses `bundle_path` as-is. Confirmed broken on Android mobile 2.39.0. The desktop webapp is unaffected due to the client-side rewrite above.

**Suggested fix:** correct the server-side path in `ClientManifest()`. The client-side compatibility shim can remain as defense-in-depth but should no longer be load-bearing.

**Temporary workaround** (if you're hitting this in production): add a reverse-proxy rewrite from `/static/<plugin_id>/*` to `/static/plugins/<plugin_id>/*` for plugin IDs matching e.g. `com.*` or `mattermost-*`. Example Caddy snippet:
```caddyfile
@plugin_static path_regexp ps ^/static/(com\.[^/]+|mattermost-[^/]+)/(.*)$
rewrite @plugin_static /static/plugins/{re.ps.1}/{re.ps.2}
```
items.title: [Bug]: Webapp plugin manifest bundle_path omits /plugins/ segment, causing 404 on mobile clients

Currently, the Mattermost Helm chart and Operator inject sensitive values (DB DSN, S3 keys, SMTP password, etc.) as environment variables via {{secretKeyRef}}. This fails STIG V-242415 (CAT I / HIGH), which requires that Kubernetes secrets must not be passed as environment variables.

To support deployments in STIG-compliant environments, Mattermost needs product-level support for reading secrets from volume-mounted files rather than environment variables.

Two approaches to consider:

# Mount each config/secret as a discrete file (more idiomatic for k8s)
# Mount a JSON blob ({{config.json}} + {{secrets.json}} overlay) as a single file (easier to implement, allows layered config)

The latter approach would allow the application to read and layer secrets on top of its existing configuration data model. The former requires more explicit per-key support.

STIG reference: https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/kubernetes/2024-06-10/finding/V-242415
