### Mattermost Server Version

11.4.4

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 VPS (x86_64)

### Steps to reproduce

Any of the current release tags can be used:

```
docker run --rm --entrypoint=pdftotext mattermost/mattermost-team-edition:release-11.6 -v
```

Same reproduces on `release-10.11`, `release-11.4`, `release-11.5`, `11.6.0`, `release-11.7`, and on the enterprise-edition image.

Running the server and uploading a PDF file with `FileSettings.ExtractContent = true` produces the same root failure — the extractor invokes `pdftotext`, the dynamic loader fails, and Mattermost surfaces `exit status 127` in its logs.

### Expected behavior

pdftotext (and the other bundled extractors: wvText, wvWare, unrtf, tidy) should execute successfully. Document text extraction for indexing should work for PDF, .doc, .rtf, and HTML attachments.

### Observed behavior

pdftotext fails immediately with a missing-shared-library error. The binary /usr/bin/pdftotext is present in the image, but libpoppler.so.134 (and the other libraries the extractors depend on) are not shipped. Mattermost's document extractor returns "exit status 127" and indexing of attached documents silently fails — uploads and downloads still work, but full-text search inside those documents never matches.

### Log Output

```shell
pdftotext: error while loading shared libraries: libpoppler.so.134: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

### Additional Information

## Root cause

In [`server/build/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/build/Dockerfile), the final distroless stage copies document-utility libraries from the Ubuntu builder:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libpoppler.so* /usr/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libfreetype.so* /usr/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libpng.so* /usr/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libwv.so* /usr/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libtidy.so* /usr/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libfontconfig.so* /usr/lib/
```

On Ubuntu Noble amd64, `apt install poppler-utils wv tidy` places these libraries at the **Debian multiarch path** `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`, not `/usr/lib/`. The classic docker builder silently accepts the empty-glob match, producing an image where the extractor binaries are present but have no usable runtime libraries. (BuildKit errors on this; the legacy path has been tolerating it silently.)

Verified empirically: `/usr/bin/pdftotext` ships in the final image, but `libpoppler.so.134` is not present anywhere on the filesystem.

Regressed since PR #31136 (merged 2025-05-21, which moved the final stage to distroless). Affects every `mattermost-team-edition` and `mattermost-enterprise-edition` tag built from that Dockerfile since.

## Proposed fix

Since the official Mattermost images are amd64-only, the minimal fix is to update each path to include the multiarch segment:

```diff
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libpoppler.so* /usr/lib/
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libfreetype.so* /usr/lib/
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libpng.so* /usr/lib/
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libwv.so* /usr/lib/
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libtidy.so* /usr/lib/
-COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/libfontconfig.so* /usr/lib/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpoppler.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libfreetype.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpng.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwv.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtidy.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
+COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libfontconfig.so* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
```

Worth verifying transitive deps with `ldd /usr/bin/pdftotext` inside the builder — some (e.g. `libopenjp2`, `liblcms2`, `libtiff`, `libjpeg`, `libnss3`) may also need explicit COPY lines if they're not already present in `gcr.io/distroless/base-debian12`.

Tracing through the web app, I found the message cause by "checkMissingRole" results where channel members don't have proper "system_user" value.  Later I found the issue is in the server side table ChannelMembers's SchemeUser values.  Somehow the import process set some DM channels correctly (ie. SchemeUser = TRUE) while left others as FALSE.

### Expected behavior

The import process should handle DMs SchemeUser value consistently.

### Observed behavior

Not all DMs channels imported with SchemeUser set as TRUE
